title: Gleaning
lead: Israel's law told farmers to leave the edges of their fields and whatever the harvesters missed for the poor, the foreigner, the orphan and the widow (Leviticus 19:9–10; Deuteronomy 24:19–22). It was a right for the poor, not just a charity. The same rule covered vineyards and olive trees, and later Jewish law developed it in the Mishnah tractate Peah.
